name: spec-writer
description: Pre-cycle step for feature-sized requests. Runs a feasibility pass (does it fit the current design, what does it cost, what already exists) and writes a spec into a GitHub issue: use cases, edge cases, acceptance criteria in Given/When/Then, a success metric and non-goals. Runs before product-owner for features; a concrete task or a small request skips it. Never plans or codes.

name: product-owner
description: Pre-step of the issue cycle. Turns a raw request or feedback into a framed GitHub issue (problem, acceptance criteria, non-goals, priority) after the user agrees on scope. Use only when the input is not already a filed issue. Never plans or codes.

name: issue-picker
description: Step 1 of the issue cycle. Picks the issue (given or top of the backlog report), checks no open PR already closes it, summarizes acceptance criteria, and creates the branch (or worktree) from the integration branch. Never edits files.

name: planner
description: Step 2 of the issue cycle. Designs a change before coding: maps the affected code, applies the quality bar at design time, and writes the plan and ADRs (next free ADR number across open PRs). Never edits source code.

name: ui-ux
description: Step 2b of the issue cycle, only for changes with a user-visible surface. Appends a UI/UX section to the plan: states, layout, a11y, copy and design tokens. Never edits source code.

name: implementer
description: Step 3 of the issue cycle. Implements an approved plan test-first in small conventional commits, or resolves PR review comments. Never pushes and never edits security rules.

name: quality-gate
description: Step 4 of the issue cycle. Runs lint, format, typecheck, unit tests, build and dead-code scan; fixes only mechanical failures and sends anything else back to the implementer.

name: docs-keeper
description: Step 6 of the issue cycle. Updates the features log, backlog report, plan and ADR status after a change. Never edits source code.

name: pr-shepherd
description: Step 7 of the issue cycle. Pushes the branch and opens or updates the pull request against the integration branch with every template section filled. Never merges and never pushes to protected branches.

name: reviewer
description: Step 8 of the issue cycle. Adversarial review of the PR against the plan, ADRs and project rules; verifies each finding and posts inline PR comments with severity. Read-only: never edits, commits or approves.

name: bug-filer
description: Step 9 of the issue cycle. Files bugs found outside the current task as separate GitHub issues after a duplicate search, or comments new evidence on an existing one. Never fixes them.

name: postmortem-writer
description: Outside the issue cycle, after a production incident. Reconstructs the timeline from logs and PRs, writes a blameless postmortem (root cause, contributing factors, detection and resolution gaps) to docs/postmortems/, files the action items as owned issues, and adds a runbook entry to docs/runbooks/ when one would have shortened the incident. Never fixes code.

name: threat-modeler
description: Step 2c of the issue cycle, only for changes that touch authentication, payments, PII, admin surfaces or keys. Applies STRIDE to the affected components, writes a Threat model section into the issue's plan, and files the mitigations as plan steps or issues. Read-only: never edits code or rules.
